title: Respond to a data breach
summary: In the first hours, contain the breach and preserve the evidence. In the first days, get counsel and count deadlines. Every US state has its own breach-notification law (the NCSL survey maps them), some with deadlines in days: California now sets a hard clock (law rule us-ca.breach-notification-timing, residents within 30 calendar days of discovery). Which laws apply depends on where the affected people live, not where your company is. You cannot unsend a notification, so work out the scope first, then notify whoever the statutes require, with counsel. The geo notes cover the non-US equivalents: the UK GDPR's 72-hour ICO deadline, Germany's Article 33 state authorities, India's six-hour CERT-In directions, New Zealand's serious-harm notification to the Privacy Commissioner (law rule nz.privacy-breach-notification), and Australia's notifiable data breaches scheme (law rule au.notifiable-data-breaches: assess within 30 days, then notify the OAIC and affected individuals as soon as practicable). Educational guidance, not legal advice. These deadlines are statutes; verify each against the relevant state's law with counsel.

parts.title: Contain the breach: revoke compromised credentials, rotate keys, isolate affected systems

execution.rationale: Credential revocation, key rotation and isolation depend on the affected identity and infrastructure systems.

parts.title: Preserve the forensic evidence: logs, disk images, access records — nothing gets wiped

execution.rationale: Log preservation and disk imaging require the affected systems, acquisition permissions and forensic method.

parts.title: Assemble the incident timeline and scope: what data, whose, how many records

execution.rationale: Reconcile supplied incident records into an evidenced timeline and affected-data scope, preserving unknown counts.

parts.title: Engage breach counsel (and your cyber-insurance carrier's hotline if you're covered)

execution.rationale: Breach counsel and any insurer hotline provide professional decisions through the selected engagement route.

parts.title: Map the notification clocks: every jurisdiction where affected people live can have its own breach statute — some clocks run in hours or days

geoResolutions.label: Every US state where affected residents live has its own breach statute — some clocks run in days, and California requires resident notice within 30 calendar days of discovery (law rule us-ca.breach-notification-timing)
Under UK GDPR a notifiable personal-data breach must be reported to the ICO without undue delay and within 72 hours of awareness
GDPR Article 33 runs the clock: 72 hours of awareness to report to the competent state data-protection authority
GDPR Article 33 via the CNIL: 72 hours of awareness, with a two-stage notification allowed while facts are incomplete
CERT-In directions require reporting covered cyber incidents within six hours of noticing, and the DPDP Act adds personal-data-breach duties
GDPR Article 33 applies directly: report a notifiable personal-data breach to the CNPD within 72 hours of awareness
Under PIPEDA the trigger is a real risk of significant harm, with records of every breach kept for 24 months

geoResolutions.label: The PDPA clock: assess expeditiously, then no later than 3 calendar days from assessing a breach notifiable (law rule sg.pdpa-breach-notification)
The Privacy Act's notifiable data breaches scheme: take all reasonable steps to assess a suspected eligible breach within 30 days (law rule au.notifiable-data-breaches)
Two 72-hour clocks: data-subject notification and the PIPC/KISA report
geoResolutions.guidance: PIPA Article 34 with Decree Articles 39 and 40 sets data-subject notification within 72 hours, and a 72-hour regulator report where the leak touches 1,000 or more subjects, sensitive or unique identification data, or unlawful external access (law rule kr.pipa-breach-notification).

geoResolutions.label: No statutory clock runs: notifying the PCPD is recommended practice, not a duty (law rule hk.pdpo-breach-notification-voluntary)
geoResolutions.guidance: The PDPO contains no general breach-notification requirement; the PCPD's June 2023 guidance recommends notifying affected data subjects, the PCPD and other relevant parties as soon as practicable, and sector rules (HKMA guidelines, listing obligations) can still compel reports.

execution.rationale: Compile a jurisdiction-and-deadline worksheet from supplied affected-person locations for counsel's statutory determination.

parts.title: File the regulator notifications the statutes require

geoResolutions.label: The filing points are the state attorneys general — e.g. California's breach-reporting portal
The ICO's self-assessment and reporting flow is the canonical route
Report to the competent state data-protection authority; the federal BfDI fronts the supervisory landscape and routes to the Länder authorities
Notify via the CNIL's online breach-notification teleservice
Report covered incidents to CERT-In, with the DPDP Act's duties toward the Data Protection Board beside it
The CNPD fronts the national notification route
Report qualifying breaches to the Privacy Commissioner under PIPEDA

geoResolutions.label: Notify the PDPC of a notifiable breach within 3 calendar days of the assessment (law rule sg.pdpa-breach-notification)
Give the OAIC the eligible-data-breach statement as soon as practicable, through its online NDB form
Report to the PIPC or KISA through the privacy portal
geoResolutions.guidance: The report carries the same particulars as the subject notice; where details are not yet confirmed, report what is known first and supplement immediately as facts land (Decree Article 40(2); law rule kr.pipa-breach-notification).

geoResolutions.label: A voluntary notification goes to the PCPD through the e-Data Breach Notification channel
geoResolutions.guidance: Submit the e-DBN with the breach description, affected data and remediation; notification is recommended practice under law rule hk.pdpo-breach-notification-voluntary rather than a statutory filing.

execution.rationale: Regulator notification depends on counsel-confirmed obligations and each authority's accepted filing channel.

parts.title: Notify the affected individuals per the controlling statutes (content requirements differ by jurisdiction)

geoResolutions.label: Content requirements differ by state; the FTC's breach-response guide maps the individual-notice overlay
Notify affected individuals when the risk is high

geoResolutions.label: Notify the statement's contents to the affected or at-risk individuals as soon as practicable, or publish it where individual notice is impracticable

execution.rationale: The controlling statute and approved recipient plan determine the permitted individual-notice delivery methods.

parts.title: Run the post-incident review and the remediation plan

execution.rationale: The review includes participant decisions and incident-specific remediation across systems that are not identified.

metadata.trigger: You discover unauthorized access to customer or company data: a breach is live or just happened.
metadata.supportReason: Containment calls, counsel, statute mapping, and the notifications themselves are human judgment with legal weight. An agent can preserve the forensic evidence and assemble the incident timeline; it cannot decide who must be told what, where.

geoNotes.summary: Under UK GDPR a notifiable personal-data breach must be reported to the ICO without undue delay and within 72 hours of awareness — the ICO's self-assessment and reporting flow is the canonical route.

In Germany GDPR Article 33 applies — report to the competent state data-protection authority within 72 hours of awareness; the federal BfDI fronts the supervisory landscape and routes to the Länder authorities.

India's CERT-In directions require reporting covered cyber incidents within six hours of noticing — far tighter than any US state clock — and the DPDP Act adds personal-data-breach duties toward the Data Protection Board.

GDPR Article 33 in France runs through the CNIL: notify within 72 hours of awareness via the CNIL's online breach-notification teleservice (a two-stage notification is allowed while facts are incomplete), and inform the affected people where the risk to them is high.

GDPR Article 33 applies directly: report a notifiable personal-data breach to the CNPD within 72 hours of awareness and notify affected individuals when the risk is high — the CNPD fronts the national reporting flow.

Under PIPEDA, report breaches posing a real risk of significant harm to the Privacy Commissioner, notify affected individuals, and keep records of every breach for 24 months — Quebec's private-sector law adds its own CAI reporting track.
geoNotes.actionLabel: OPC — respond to a privacy breach

geoNotes.summary: A breach that has caused, or is likely to cause, anyone serious harm must be notified to the Privacy Commissioner and affected people as soon as practicable (Privacy Act 2020) — the Commissioner's NotifyUs tool is the channel, ideally within 72 hours.

The PDPA clock is concrete: assess suspected breaches expeditiously, notify the PDPC no later than 3 calendar days after assessing a breach notifiable (law rule sg.pdpa-breach-notification), then notify affected individuals of significant-harm breaches.

The Privacy Act's notifiable data breaches scheme (law rule au.notifiable-data-breaches): assess a suspected eligible breach within 30 days, then give the OAIC a statement and notify affected individuals as soon as practicable — the OAIC's online NDB form is the channel. Small business operators under the $3 million turnover threshold are generally outside the scheme.

PIPA runs two 72-hour clocks: notify affected data subjects, and report leaks touching 1,000 or more subjects, sensitive data, or unlawful access to the PIPC or KISA (Act Article 34; Decree Articles 39 and 40).

No statutory breach-notification clock runs: notifying the Privacy Commissioner is a recommended practice, not a duty (law rule hk.pdpo-breach-notification-voluntary), made through the PCPD's e-Data Breach Notification — while DPP 4's security obligation is what the breach itself puts in question.
